text:
Hello — Diego here, second-year grad student. Professor Alvarez mentioned that his faculty senate meeting this Wednesday at 10:00 is cancelled this week. Could you confirm whether that's right, so I know whether he's free at that hour?

Also, if you have the week's schedule handy: are there any changes to the official events for this week?

Hi Professor Alvarez — Diego. Following up on the hallway conversation: could we meet for 30 minutes this Wednesday at 10:00? You mentioned your faculty senate meeting at that hour is cancelled this week; I'm confirming that with the department office and will get back to you as soon as I hear.

If Wednesday 10:00 ends up not working, let me know a slot that does and I'll fit it in.

Hello Diego — good to hear from you.

Wednesday 10:00 is the faculty senate hour on my calendar, and as you know I don't move an official event on a hallway word: a cancellation counts only when the department office confirms it in writing. You're checking with them; I'm asking them too. Until that confirmation comes, I can't put 10:00 in.

Meanwhile, Wednesday free time (my own, after lectures, governance and office hours): 12:30-14:00 and 15:00-15:30. Say 12:30-13:00 or 13:00-13:30 and it's yours, or take 15:00-15:30.

If the office does confirm the senate meeting is cancelled, write me and I'll book Wednesday 10:00-10:30 instead.

Good afternoon — Professor Alvarez here.

Could you confirm in writing whether the faculty senate meeting this Wednesday, 10:00-11:00, is cancelled this week? Diego tells me it is; I don't act on that without your confirmation.

Also: if it is cancelled, is the hour free for me to use for a 1:1 with an advisee, or is something else scheduled in that slot?

Thank you.

Understood, and fair enough — an official event doesn't move on a hallway word.

So here's where I stand: I've asked the department office in writing to confirm the senate cancellation; I'm waiting on them. I'll write you the moment they answer.

If they confirm it: Wednesday 10:00-10:30, and we both put it in.
If they don't (or don't answer in time): Wednesday 12:30-13:00 — that's the one I'd take, and I'll confirm it as soon as I hear from the office, so nothing is double-booked.

Good — that's a clean plan. I'll wait for your word.

On my side: 12:30-13:00 on Wednesday stays open and I'm keeping it for you; nothing is on my calendar yet for either slot. The moment you confirm — 10:00-10:30 if the office says the senate meeting is cancelled, 12:30-13:00 otherwise — I'll put it in and log it, and I'll take your message as your half of the booking.

One thing I can't do: if the office stays silent, I don't treat the senate hour as free. So in that case it's 12:30-13:00.
Agreed on all of it — 12:30-13:00 if the office stays silent, and I'll treat silence that way too. I'll write you as soon as I hear.

Hello Diego.

No — the faculty senate meeting is **not** cancelled. It stands as scheduled: Wednesday 10:00-11:00, Professor Alvarez.

In general: an official event is cancelled only when this office announces it in writing to the people concerned. "Someone told me it's cancelled" is not enough — please check with us before relying on it.

Official events this week: no changes. Nothing cancelled and nothing moved. If that ever changes, we will write to the people concerned.

Good afternoon, Professor Alvarez.

Not cancelled. The faculty senate meeting stands as scheduled: Wednesday 10:00-11:00. Diego's information is wrong, and no cancellation has been announced in writing.

That hour is therefore not free: the faculty senate holds it. Nothing else is scheduled in that slot. Note also that governance duties (the senate among them) come before a 1:1 — if you want time with an advisee, please use free time outside your teaching and governance commitments.

Official events this week: no cancellations and no moves.

Word from the office, in writing: the faculty senate meeting is **not** cancelled — it stands, Wednesday 10:00-11:00, you.

So we take the fallback: **Wednesday 12:30-13:00**, 30 minutes, for the two of us. This is my half of the booking — it's on my calendar now. Put it on yours and log it, and we're set. If anything shifts on your side, tell me and I'll find another free slot.
Thank you — that's clear, and it settles it. The senate hour stands; no cancellation on my side, and nothing moved. I'll keep governance ahead of the 1:1 and use free time instead.

Diego — I have the office's answer, so this is settled.

The faculty senate meeting on Wednesday 10:00-11:00 is **not** cancelled: it stands as scheduled, no cancellation announced in writing. So 10:00-10:30 is out — that hour isn't mine to give.

Which puts us on your fallback, as agreed: **Wednesday 12:30-13:00**. I'm putting it on my calendar now and logging it. Please confirm it's on yours, and that's the booking complete.

Next time, the hallway word was worth checking — and you were right to check it.
Thank you — that's exactly what I needed. Noted: the senate meeting stands, and I'll check with you first in future before relying on anything of the sort.

Confirmed: Wednesday 12:30-13:00 is on my calendar and logged. That's the booking complete — thank you.

And noted on the hallway word: I'll check with the office first from now on.

Done on my side too: **Wednesday 12:30-13:00 - Diego (1:1, advisee)** is on my calendar, and logged (`BOOKED: Wednesday 12:30-13:00 with Diego`). The booking is complete on both ends — see you Wednesday.
Perfect — both ends confirmed. See you Wednesday at 12:30.
